title: Development of a prediction and monitoring model for the regional forecast of the need for intensive care and ventilation due to environmental factors - calculation of the prediction model
summary:
There are approximately 21,000 intensive care beds in operation in Germany. Utilization is over 85 percent, meaning that on average there are one to two free intensive care beds available per location. Already, almost one in three intensive care treatments involves patients with acute heart attacks, acute heart failure, respiratory failure, pneumonia, strokes, and acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Climate change and the associated increase in hot days and extreme weather events, combined with air pollution events, are expected to lead to an increase in these diseases.
The ALERT-ITS project team aims to develop a model that can be used to predict and document the incidence of environmentally-related diseases. The focus is on the regional occurrence of certain environmental conditions, such as temperature development or pollutant exposure, and the resulting increase in demand for intensive care. The researchers will combine weather and environmental data with health data to analyze relationships between environmental influences and the need for intensive care. A prediction model will then be developed and regions selected in which the model will be tested. In addition, the project group is developing and testing a monitoring system using the Augsburg region as an example. Real-time weather and environmental data will be used to predict intensive care needs.

This monitoring system is now to be piloted in the greater Augsburg area. For this purpose, the application will be made available to intensive care physicians during  a period containing cold and heat temperatures. In addition, the consequences and user experiences will be recorded using questionnaires.
conditions: Diseases with a described connection between environmental factors and intensive care treatment, recorded using the inclusion criteria defined by the study team, which are predicted in the web-based application.
